root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Gubinsky-Melts Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6

overview: Black retreats the queen to d6 rather than a5, keeping it central and the a5 square free for ...a6 or ...Nf6. After 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 Black builds a ...c6/...e6 or ...a6 structure and a Caro-Kann-like position. White has more space and a lead in development; Black stays solid but must avoid traps on the d-file.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4, Nf3 and Bd2 or Bf4/Bb5 to harass the queen on d6
Use the space and development lead; Nb5 and Bf4 ideas against the queen

black_ideas.idea: ...Nf6, ...a6, ...Bg4 or ...Bf5 and ...e6; keep the structure sound and use ...c5 or ...e5
Develop quickly and neutralise the early queen exposure

typical_structures.structure: White d4 centre against Black c6/e6 or ...a6 set-up; Scandinavian semi-open d-file

character.notes: Quiet, solid Scandinavian development; Black's position is hard to break down but the queen on d6 is slightly exposed.

gambit.notes: Black has already regained the pawn.

soundness.notes: Sound; White keeps a small edge.

structure.notes: Fixed asymmetric centre with the d-file semi-open for Black; Scandinavian standard is semi-open.

approach.notes: A respectable, if less common, queen retreat; some strong players use it.

level.notes: Few concrete lines, but handling the exposed queen takes judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Schiller main line
sublines_that_differ.how: Black prevents Nb5 and sets up ...Bg4 or ...c5.

character.reason: Few ways to lose quickly and Black's position is hard to attack.

structure.reason: Scandinavian: asymmetric centre with half-open d-file.

level.reason: Needs care with the exposed queen but low theory.

plans.reason: Black's queen sits in the centre and has to avoid being harried.
